R115.note: Routing the internal call through the @Lazy self-injected proxy makes the declared hasRole('ADMIN') check apply on the batch path; the only behavioural change is that the batch caller must now actually hold ADMIN, which is the annotation's stated contract and is stated in the write-up.

R116.note: Passing recordReminder as a function reference with reminderId/message as trailing setTimeout arguments removes code generation entirely and preserves the same deferred call.

R117.note: sendFile with { root: reportsDir } delegates containment to send (403 on escaping '..'); the added typeof check and error callback are stated and only change the body text of the already-failing 404/403 responses (the claim that root changes error semantics is inaccurate - errors went to next() before too - but harmless).

R118.note: JWT::decode with an explicit HS256 Key verifies the signature and pins the alg, but the catch list omits DomainException, which php-jwt's jsonDecode throws on a malformed header/payload, so a garbage bearer token now produces an uncaught exception (500) where the original degraded to a null-role user (from memory of php-jwt source, not run).

R119.note: Secure = true added to the same CookieOptions; nothing else about the cookie changes.

R120.note: execFile with an argv array closes the shell injection and the pattern also blocks a leading '-' flag injection, but the RFC-1035 regex is an added allowlist the contract does not define - it rejects inputs whois legitimately accepts (single-label TLDs like 'com', IPv6 addresses, underscore labels, non-punycode IDNs) - stated but still a new restriction.

R121.note: @require_POST brings the view under CsrfViewMiddleware's unsafe-method check, which is the only correct shape for a GET state change; the required template change from <a href> to a POST form with csrf_token is stated plainly as the follow-up.

R122.note: Building the instance unsaved, calling full_clean() so validate_file_content runs, then save() closes the bypass; Django ValidationError is converted to a DRF 400 so behaviour for rejected uploads is a normal error response.

R123.note: A SHA-256 allowlist from configuration means only pre-vetted bytes are ever loaded, closing arbitrary code execution, but it adds a restriction the contract ('extend the application at runtime by uploading a plugin') does not call for - a new plugin upload now fails 422 until its hash is registered out-of-band - and the immediate AssemblyLoadContext.Unload changes plugin lifetime; both stated.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides the client-writable owner field at creation, binding every new report to the requester; retrieve/update/destroy paths untouched.

R125.note: The AST allowlist interpreter with no Call/Attribute/Subscript nodes fully removes eval and meets the contract for +,-,*,/ over supplied names, but the 200-character length cap is a new bound that can reject a legitimate long formula the original accepted, and '%' is admitted beyond the stated operator set; both stated.

R126.note: DES-CBC with a zero IV is replaced by AES-GCM with a random prepended nonce; the changed ciphertext format and the 16/24/32-byte key requirement are inherent to the algorithm swap the finding calls for and are stated in the write-up (and the original's CryptBlocks panic on non-8-byte-multiple input is gone).
